summary: configuration.py is passive: it defines immutable product, runtime, and subscription snapshots plus explicit environment/file loaders and atomic product-cache persistence. Importing it constructs no REST client, OrderBook, or process-global runtime resource; main.py owns composition.

The two retained browser operator clients are the stealth-order manager and span builder. Both use the same strict JSON-RPC envelope, UUID correlation, bootstrap gate, named projections, and client_order_id wire vocabulary; abandoned pages and the terminal console are not supported entrypoints.

summary: dashboard_server.py is the embedded operator adapter: main.py installs the shared OrderBook and ExecutionCore, strict operator_api framing feeds one explicit JSON-RPC dispatch map, and method-correlated schema validation gates every success payload. New sockets are notification-barred; a successful bootstrap response is sent first, followed by targeted fresh runtime and stealth catch-up before ordinary live fanout opens. A handler's terminal response precedes independently best-effort requested projections, including recovery publication after a producer-contract error. The adapter still coordinates application handlers and reads, remains an unauthenticated plain-WebSocket listener, and is not a standalone runtime.
FeeManager and ProfitValidator own fee freshness/regime inputs, target derivation, and profitability decisions.

Execution Core stages 5.1-5.4B.4 form the transport-neutral application boundary. The facade exposes typed lifecycle controls, caller-owned stealth snapshots, and six explicit strategy-originating commands; each originating call crosses one atomic application-command admission scope before delegating lifecycle work to existing owners. Consumer-owned persistence, projection, and hook protocols remove fill-ledger and event-stream database access, the bridge span parent-row import, the cancelled-parent move manager database import, and dashboard and registry lookup from execution owners; main.py composes one concrete persistence adapter.

Integration registries expose dynamic WebSocket, placement, fill, and stealth lifecycle callbacks; OrderEventStreamPublisher is a principal subscriber. The retained stealth lifecycle callback runs synchronously and suppresses subscriber failures for best-effort auditing; no generic order-state/inventory registry remains.

Hotpoint modules detect clustered fill activity, rate-limit automatic replication, place orders only for source strategies with per-strategy enable_hotpoint_replication enabled, and sweep decayed open auto-placements. Auto-placed rows disable replication to prevent cascades.
Market tick recording, metrics, and candle storage retain local market history and derived runtime state; the abandoned operator chart/calibration query helpers are not part of the supported surface.

The source-only modular-monolith contract classifies every supported runtime module, permits only declared zone directions, and freezes 16 reverse-zone edges, zero runtime import cycles, 34 broad or untyped constructor capability surfaces, and seven reflection or namespace escape signatures. Exact debt baselines must shrink deliberately or expand only after architecture review; the contract does not prove arbitrary runtime aliases or dynamic dispatch.

MoveManager owns parent-order eligibility, manual replacement-parent creation, move history, premarking, and cancel-triggered pending moves behind CancelledOrderMovePersistence. Automatic pending completion uses one exact-row atomic canonical helper and caches the root only after commit; it does not place a live exchange order. Manual replacement creation and audit insertion remain separate helper transactions.

operator_api owns strict JSON-RPC 2.0 framing plus complete version-one method-param/result and notification schemas. It accepts one correlated canonical-UUID request at a time, rejects unsupported or malformed input, validates each JSON-normalized handler result against its originating method before success emission, and exposes notification validators for boundary tests while the schema remains the future binding contract; lifecycle and persistence remain outside this package.

OrderEngine is the central Coinbase transport and order-lifecycle host. It owns public websocket ingress, persistence, and lifecycle routing, while one UserFeedProcessor owns authenticated reduction and bounded keyed dispatch. Its single user-order path preserves guarded execution-owner projection and factual fill/audit ingestion. Fill-ledger, event-stream, and cancelled-parent move persistence, dashboard publication, and WebSocket, fill, placement, and lifecycle hooks are narrow injected capabilities; the engine does not import their concrete adapters.
OrderProgressTracker converts cumulative WebSocket snapshots into monotonic deltas and protects per-order watermark and follow-up claims.

database.order is the canonical schema and write/read surface for order lineage, durable execution ownership, atomic placement/logical status projection, stealth state, moves, fills, event audit, conditions, and partial-fill progress. Its schema import boundary uses core constants directly and does not initialize live runtime configuration.

core.orderbook.OrderBook is the sole runtime in-memory authority for orders, parent/child links, positions, product/reference data, and follow-up claims. It owns one RLock and exposes explicit snapshots, mutators, product resolution, and metadata readers; configuration has no OrderBook shim or global instance.
PostgresDB provides lazy psycopg2 connection management and serializes each cursor transaction on one process-local RLock.
calculation.price_validation and size_validation are the shared product-metadata-aware normalization boundaries used before order persistence/submission.

main.py is the sole process composition root: it loads one settings snapshot and constructs the REST adapter, product catalog, shared OrderBook, manager, bridge, Execution Core facade, engine, one shared database persistence adapter, dashboard projection sink, shared hook registries, and reconcilers before owning fail-closed startup and cooperative shutdown.
StartupReconciler compares exchange and local state through an injected read-only REST capability; PeriodicReconciler owns and reuses that same adapter for background audits.

RuntimeController owns initial fail-closed STARTING, sticky startup pause and readiness completion, coherent lifecycle snapshots, lock-free signal stop intent, admission and atomic terminal in-flight accounting, named level-triggered admission-open hooks invoked outside controller locks, bounded startup-component registration/start, lifecycle-aware stop hooks, and single-owner logical drain to STOPPED.

StealthOrderBridge connects ticker data and runtime admission to stealth evaluation, reveal, repricing, and periodic memory hydration. It consumes a required SpanParentOrderReader for canonical parent-row validation while all deterministic span rung locks are held. It serializes terminal rearm consumption under per-order action locks and recovers persisted pending_rearm intents by exact same-order REST truth during activation and the existing reconciliation loop; DB hydration and schedule construction remain interruptible outside its lifecycle lock and bounded worker publication is serialized against sticky stop. Manual Rehide retains readiness and per-order action locking after ExecutionCore admission, while manual move now has an explicit typed bridge operation rather than transport reach-through to the manager. Source-SID guards order follow-up creation and intentional cancellation while existing children remain independent.

StealthEventDeadlineScheduler owns the sole ordered market-event FIFO and generational monotonic deadline heap. One worker dispatches market snapshots and current-generation wakes; lifecycle and persistence truth remain in StealthOrderManager.

StealthOrderManager owns local stealth lifecycle, condition state, reveal placement, root strategy resolution, repricing, move/rehide, cancellation, and persistence. Children retain independent execution state while root definitions govern strategy. Placement and best-effort lifecycle callbacks use injected typed capabilities rather than integration singleton lookup; their established ordering and failure policy remain unchanged.

The complete Linux non-external gate covers root tests plus unit, integration, e2e, and mandatory regression suites, including modular-boundary, fresh-database, and paused-deployment automation contracts. Pytest forces the isolated port-9876 PostgreSQL target, provisions its schema before collection, and rejects localhost production-port access by default. scripts/validate_release.sh wraps the suite with graph, diff, and clean-worktree checks; external tests remain opt-in.

UserFeedProcessor is the instance-owned authenticated-feed boundary. It owns connection generations, sequence and bootstrap state, the ordered reducer, bounded per-client_order_id FIFO dispatch, reconnect fencing, and operational metrics while calling OrderEngine through the explicit UserFeedHost protocol.
